description.la: Epistolae S. Bernardi, CDLX, ordine Mabillonii, cum epistolis ad eum scriptis quae inter eas typis expressae sunt. Textus ex editione Migne (Patrologia Latina 182, 1854).
description.en-US: The 460 letters of Bernard of Clairvaux in Mabillon’s numbering, as printed in the Maurist text of Migne (Patrologia Latina 182, 1854): to popes, kings, bishops, monks and friends, each headed with its addressee and Mabillon’s summary, with a few letters to Bernard (Peter the Venerable’s reply, Eugene III’s letter to the Cistercian chapter) that Mabillon prints among them. Latin from a machine-corrected OCR. Letters 42 (On the conduct and office of bishops), 77 (On baptism) and 190 (Against the errors of Abelard) are the treatises Mabillon moved to the second tome; they are given here as letters. The English is Samuel J. Eales's (Life and Works of Saint Bernard, 1889–1896), with his notes: his numbering follows the Latin to 419, and the letters he adds (charters, letters to Bernard, and those found by Hüffer and others) follow the Latin as an English-only group.
description.pt-BR: As 460 cartas de Bernardo de Claraval, na numeração de Mabillon, a monges, bispos, papas, reis e amigos.

la.editor: Jean Mabillon, in J.-P. Migne (Patrologia Latina 182)

sources.edition: S. Bernardi Claraevallensis abbatis opera omnia, ed. J. Mabillon, in Migne, Patrologia Latina 182 (Paris 1854), Epistolae; TEI XML of the Corpus Corporum (University of Zurich), text 21392, from machine-corrected OCR.
sources.description: All letters I-CDLX with their summaries (in italics) and Mabillon’s monita. PL page breaks, columns and the paragraph numbers are dropped. Where the printed numeral repeats a number and skips the next (the second CXX and CCXXI), the skipped number is restored (CXXI, CCXXIX).
sources.tierEvidence: Bernard died in 1153; Migne’s 1854 printing is public domain everywhere.

sources.edition: Life and Works of Saint Bernard, Abbot of Clairvaux, ed. Dom John Mabillon, translated and edited with additional notes by Samuel J. Eales: vols. 1-2, second edition (London: Burns & Oates, n.d.; archive.org saintbernardlife00bernuoft, saintbernardlife02bernuoft), letters I-CCCLXXX; vol. 3 (London: John Hodges, 1896; archive.org lifeworksofsaint03bern), letters CCCLXXXI-CDXC.
sources.description: Archive.org OCR read from the word-coordinate files and cleaned by script, not proofread: running heads, page numbers and signature marks dropped, the translator's footnotes told from the text by their type and placed at their marker (or, where the OCR lost the marker, at the end of the text of their page). Eales's numbering is the Latin's for letters 1-419; his 420-454 are Latin 421-455, his 455 is Latin 420, and his 485-488 are Latin 457-460, so those chapters carry a line giving his number. His 456-484, 489 and 490 (charters, letters to Bernard, and the appendix of letters found since Mabillon) have no Latin here and are English-only chapters. Latin 456 (to Raymond, a doubtful letter) has no English. Letters 42 and 77 are given by Eales only as a note sending the reader to the treatises.
sources.tierEvidence: Eales died in 1910; the volumes were printed 1889-1896: public domain in the US.
